package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of the xz package (5.6.0 and 5.6.1) contain a sophisticated backdoor that allows attackers to bypass SSH authentication, granting unauthorized remote access. The malicious code is hidden in binary test files and leverages glibc's IFUNC mechanism to intercept and subvert cryptographic operations, specifically targeting the sshd process. This is a deliberate supply chain attack, with the malicious code introduced by a trusted contributor over a long period.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when sshd is running and liblzma is loaded)
execution_context.file_location: liblzma (part of xz package), with payload hidden in binary test files within the source distribution

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious code is embedded in two binary test files, which are loaded by the build process and ultimately included in the liblzma library. The code leverages glibc's IFUNC (indirect function) mechanism to hook into cryptographic routines used by sshd, allowing the attacker to bypass authentication checks.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hooks into sshd's cryptographic routines via glibc IFUNC, intercepts authentication logic, and allows unauthorized access by bypassing normal SSH authentication, resulting in remote root access for the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and subverting authentication routines in a core system library is highly abnormal and enables privilege escalation and unauthorized access.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal compression libraries should not interact with authentication processes or hook into cryptographic routines of unrelated services like sshd.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: IFUNC is sometimes used for performance optimizations in cryptographic libraries, but never to alter authentication logic or bypass security controls.
key_indicators: Use of glibc IFUNC to hook system calls
Binary payloads hidden in test files
Code only active in specific runtime contexts (sshd, glibc)

execution_context.trigger: build-time and runtime (when building and loading the library)
execution_context.file_location: Binary test files embedded in the xz source distribution
required_permissions: filesystem (to read and load binary files)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The malicious payload is split across two binary test files, which are not source code but are loaded and executed as part of the build and runtime process. These files contain encrypted code that is decrypted and executed by the main library under certain conditions.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time and runtime, the library loads and decrypts code from binary test files, then executes it in-process, enabling the backdoor logic to be injected into the running sshd process.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Embedding executable payloads in binary test files is a classic obfuscation and evasion technique, especially when the files are not expected to contain code.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Test files in a compression library should contain only data for testing compression/decompression, not executable code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Test files may contain compressed data for regression tests, but not encrypted code meant for execution.
key_indicators: Test files used as code delivery mechanism
Decryption and execution of binary blobs at runtime

attack_chain.action: Malicious contributor (Jia Tan) introduces binary test files containing encrypted payloads into the xz source code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is present in the distributed source and binary packages.

attack_chain.action: During build and installation, the xz/liblzma library loads and decrypts the payload from the binary test files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is included in the built library and ready to execute at runtime.

attack_chain.action: When sshd loads liblzma (directly or indirectly), the malicious code leverages glibc IFUNC to hook into cryptographic routines.
attack_chain.leads_to: Backdoor logic is injected into the sshd process.

attack_chain.action: At runtime, the backdoor intercepts SSH authentication, allowing the attacker to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker achieves remote root access to the system.

behavioral_signatures: liblzma or xz library loading unexpected binary blobs at build or runtime
Use of glibc IFUNC to hook or override cryptographic/authentication routines
Unusual slowdown in sshd authentication (e.g., increased login latency)
Presence of encrypted or non-standard binary test files in source distribution
file_indicators: Binary test files in xz/liblzma source (e.g., test/test-vectors or similar)
xz/liblzma library files with unexpected code sections or increased size
network_indicators: Unusual SSH connections or authentication bypasses
Potential C2 (command and control) connections if attacker uses the backdoor
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan for xz/liblzma package versions 5.6.0 and 5.6.1 on all systems, including containers and VMs. Inspect xz/liblzma source and binary distributions for unexpected binary test files or encrypted payloads. Monitor for use of glibc IFUNC in liblzma and for any code that hooks into sshd authentication routines. Watch for abnormal SSH authentication behavior, such as unexplained successful logins or increased authentication latency. Use SBOM tools to inventory affected packages and automate alerts for known-bad versions.
